1.pericope_label: In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness. And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land
debates: What the opened fountain stands for
Which period the promise about the idols belongs to
outliers: Calvin reports interpreters who made the fountain baptism and prefers those who made it the blood
Clarke turns the named recipients into an argument that none need despair
Ellicott notes this is the only Old Testament use of the phrase unclean spirit
themes: A spring that is never sealed shut
A rock smitten so that water might come
Idols whose very names are forgotten
A cleansing water could not accomplish

3.pericope_label: And it shall come to pass, that when any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the Lord. And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends
debates: Whether the parents kill their son or only chastise him
What the wounds in his hands are
Whether the verse may be applied to Christ at all
outliers: Clarke says he cannot hear the messianic application of the verse without horror
Ellicott would have the man claim to be a bought slave with no time for inspiration
Ellicott notes that the phrase that day here covers a period hidden from the prophet
themes: Parents turning on their own son
A hairy mantle worn as a disguise
A diviner claiming to be a herdsman

7.pericope_label: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow, saith the Lord of hosts: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered: and I will turn mine hand upon the little ones
debates: Whose sword is called to awake
What the title my fellow implies
Whether the turning of the hand is favour or judgment
outliers: Ellicott uses the title my fellow to argue the passage stands where it belongs
Clarke sets a passage of Aeschylus beside the address to the sword
Henry contrasts the sword of justice with the sword of war
themes: A sword told to wake from a long sleep
Iron acting as a cruel umpire
A rod refused where a sword is commanded
A hand turned toward the smallest of the flock

8.pericope_label: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein. And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, The Lord is my God
debates: Whether the land means Israel or the whole world
Who the surviving third part are
Whether the fractions are meant exactly
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reads these verses as explaining the promise about the little ones
Ellicott says the prophet speaks vaguely, by the analogy of a captivity already past
Wesley warns that the two parts are not precisely two
themes: A flock divided before it is scattered
A small portion given a different fate from the rest
A call answered on both sides
